# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-5062

# Review — PAN-5062
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — the documented dbt recipe treats `workspace.env.template` as a file path, but it is inline content, so agents never receive `DBT_SCHEMA`

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-5062-review-81fb25e0
- Manifest: .pan/review/agent-pan-5062-review-81fb25e0/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-5062 / workspaces/feature-pan-5062
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/5073
- HEAD reviewed: 81fb25e04facc260812183506794af1480fd8623
- Base: origin/main merge-base 5ff981f25cd; prior cycle: none

## Blocking Findings

### [requirements] dbt recipe documents `workspace.env.template` as a file path; it is inline content — `configuration/projects.mdx:254` and the recipe at `configuration/projects.mdx:~341`
- Severity: ! MUST
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect (docs deliverable), in_pr_scope (FR-7 / WI-6 / AC-6)
- Trigger and changed-code connection: The new Configuration Fields row says `workspace.env.template` is a "Path to an env template rendered to `<workspace>/.env`". The new `### dbt and data projects` example sets `template: infra/env.template` and says "`infra/env.template` renders to `<workspace>/.env`". The only reader is `src/lib/workspace-manager/create.ts:673-675`: `replacePlaceholders(workspaceConfig.env.template, placeholders)` is written verbatim with `writeFileSync(join(workspacePath, '.env'), envContent)`. The field is the template text itself (the existing `configuration/polyrepo.mdx` example uses `template: |` inline content).
- Expected / observed / impact: Expected (WI-6 spec): "a working `projects.yaml` example with `workspace.env.template: "DBT_SCHEMA=dev_{{FEATURE_IDENT}}\n"`". Observed: a user who copies the recipe gets a `.env` whose only line is `infra/env.template`. `parseWorkspaceEnv` finds no `KEY=value` line, so `env.load: true` exports nothing and the agent shell has no `DBT_SCHEMA`. An agent's `dbt build` then fails on `env_var('DBT_SCHEMA')` ("Env var required but not provided"). The gates still work because they get `DBT_SCHEMA` from `gate.env`, which masks the problem until an agent runs dbt itself. The agent half of the feature's headline recipe does not work, and the field-table row misdescribes an existing config field.
- Evidence: static trace of `create.ts:672-677` (read at HEAD); `parseWorkspaceEnv` regex `^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)=(.*)$` in `src/lib/workspace-env.ts:19` rejects a line with no `=`. Not run end to end against dbt (NFR-1: no dbt in tests).
- Fix: In `configuration/projects.mdx`, change the row to "Inline `.env` content rendered to `<workspace>/.env` at workspace creation; placeholders rendered once." In the recipe, use the inline form from the spec, e.g.
  ```yaml
  workspace:
    env:
      template: |
        DBT_SCHEMA=dev_{{FEATURE_IDENT}}
      load: true
  ```
  and replace the "`infra/env.template` renders to …" sentence to match. While there, add the `profiles.yml` dbt-duckdb snippet the spec asked for (`path: "{{ env_var('DBT_DUCKDB_PATH') }}"`, plus `DBT_DUCKDB_PATH={{WORKSPACE_PATH}}/dev.duckdb` in the template), because the current duckdb example sets only the gate env and never shows how dbt reads it.

## Non-blocking Findings

- `~` **Project-root check compares unexpanded paths** — `src/lib/workspace-env.ts:62`. `loadWorkspaceEnvForProject` uses `resolve(workspacePath) === resolve(project.path)`, but projects.yaml keeps paths as written (`~/Projects/x`, symlinked roots). `findProjectByPath` canonicalizes via `canonicalPath`, this check does not. With `env.load: true` and a project root whose own checkout has a `.env` (common for compose projects), a conversation launched at the project root would export that root `.env`. Opt-in and the file is the operator's own, so impact is bounded. Fix: compare `canonicalPath()` results from `src/lib/projects/path-containment.ts`. Classification: implementation defect, in_pr_scope, bounded.
- `?` **Launcher now reads projects.yaml when `<workingDir>/.env` exists** — `workspaceEnvLauncherLines` calls `findProjectByPath` → `loadProjectsConfigSync()`, which rethrows on malformed YAML. A launch in any workspace with a `.env` (opted in or not) would then throw from `generateLauncherScript`. Most spawn paths already load projects.yaml earlier, so a malformed file likely fails them first; not demonstrated. A try/catch returning `[]` would make it non-fatal.
- `?` **`{{HOME}}` is listed as a gate placeholder but the merge path does not set it** — `merge-ops.ts:651-662` builds `gatePlaceholders` without `HOME` (verification-runner sets it). `{{HOME}}` in `gate.env` or `command` stays literal on the merge-time gate run. Pre-existing for `command`; the new docs sentence ("accept every placeholder … `{{HOME}}`") now advertises it. Low impact.
- `≉` **Inline comments are kept in values** — `FOO=bar # note` yields `bar # note`; docker compose strips such comments. Generated templates are unlikely to contain them. Advisory.
- Spec note: FR-6 wording "before Overdeck's own exports" is accurate for agent identity/provider/PATH exports; `OVERDECK_HOME` is exported earlier but reserved `OVERDECK_*` keys are dropped by the parser, so no override is possible. No action.

### Dimensions
- **Correctness:** traced every placeholder construction site (6), gate env rendering, host/container/remote branches, launcher ordering. Only the project-root path comparison is imprecise (advisory).
- **Security:** `.env` keys constrained to identifier regex before `export`; values `shellQuote`d (bash round-trip test); file is parsed, never sourced; `OVERDECK_*`/`PATH`/`HOME` dropped; opt-in only. Container `-e K="v"` quoting unchanged (D-5, non-goal); rendered values come from operator config and issue ids. No new exposure under the trusted-local-agent model.
- **Performance:** one `existsSync` per launch, plus mtime-cached projects.yaml read only when a `.env` exists; one small file read per verification/merge gate run. No child processes, no `execSync`.
- **Requirements/UX:** see AC matrix.
